Troubleshooting

This section addresses common issues and provides solutions for the current RAPAS Photometry Pipeline workflow.

Installation & Setup Issues

Error: Python version mismatch (Expected Python 3.12)

  • Problem: The project is tested against Python 3.12, but a different Python version is active.

  • Solution:

    1. Check your Python version: python --version

    2. Install Python 3.12 from python.org or your package manager.

    3. Create a new virtual environment with Python 3.12: python3.12 -m venv .venv

    4. Activate the environment and reinstall dependencies: pip install -e .

Error: ImportError: No module named ‘…’

  • Problem: Required Python packages are not installed or are not found in the current environment.

  • Solution:

    1. Ensure your virtual environment is activated.

    2. Verify you are using Python 3.12.

    3. Run pip install -e . from the project root.

    4. If issues persist, try pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall -e ..

Error: Could not connect to the backend

  • Problem: The selected backend is not running or is inaccessible.

  • Solution:

    1. Open a separate terminal in the project root.

    2. Activate the virtual environment.

    3. Start either python -m uvicorn api.main:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 or python backend.py.

    4. Check the terminal output for errors and confirm the expected port is available.

    5. If needed, set RPP_API_URL or RPP_LEGACY_URL to match your environment.

    6. If the FastAPI server is running but GET /health returns HTTP 500 after a Python or library upgrade, treat that as a backend dependency problem rather than a missing legacy server. Reinstall the environment from the project root with pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall -e . and verify that anyio was reinstalled cleanly.

Error: ``FastAPI.__call__() missing 1 required positional argument: ‘send’``

  • Problem: The FastAPI app was started with plain Gunicorn WSGI workers, for example gunicorn api.main:app, so requests such as GET /health fail before they reach FastAPI.

  • Solution:

    1. Start the API with Uvicorn directly: python -m uvicorn api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000.

    2. Or start it with Gunicorn using the ASGI worker: gunicorn -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api.main:app.

    3. If you launch Gunicorn from the project root, the repository’s gunicorn.conf.py now sets uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker by default.

Error: DLL load failed while importing… (Windows)

  • Problem: Missing C++ runtime libraries required by some Python packages.

  • Solution: Install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable packages for Visual Studio from the official Microsoft website.

Login & Registration Issues

Error: “Username or email is already taken.”

  • Problem: The chosen username or email address already exists in the database.

  • Solution: Choose a different username and/or email address.

Error: “Invalid username or password.”

  • Problem: Incorrect password, or an identifier that does not match any account.

  • Solution:

    1. The Login field accepts the account username or the email address used at registration. Try the email if you no longer remember the username.

    2. Verify the password, and use the password recovery option if you forgot it.

Where can I see who logged in?

  • Solution: every successful login writes a timestamped line with the pipeline version to the service log, for example [2026-10-18 18:46:22] RPP v1.9.0 - User 'intern1' logged in successfully (FastAPI backend). The FastAPI backend, the legacy backend and the frontend each emit their own line, so a login appears in both the backend and frontend logs. Administrators can also open the in-app Pipeline Logs page (pages/showlogs.py) to read the last 200 lines of fastapi_backend.log and streamlit_frontend.log.

Error: “Email already registered.” while the account cannot be reached

  • Problem: The address is already attached to an account, but the login identifier does not match it.

  • Solution:

    1. Log in with the email address itself instead of a username.

    2. Reset the password through Password Recovery, then log in with the email address and the new password.

Password Recovery Fails / No Email Received

  • Problem: Email sending is not configured correctly on the backend.

  • Solution:

    1. Ensure the active backend is running.

    2. Verify that SMTP settings are correctly configured, especially SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, and SMTP_PASS_ENCODED.

    3. Check the backend terminal output for email sending errors.

    4. Check your email spam folder.

    5. Ensure your email provider allows sending via SMTP.

Note

For privacy, the recovery request always reports success, even when no account uses the submitted address. The address must therefore be exactly the one attached to an account. Matching ignores capitalisation and surrounding spaces, so any spelling of the address that resolves to the registered mailbox works.

Image Loading & Processing Issues

Error: Could not read FITS file / No image data found

  • Problem: The file is corrupted, not a valid FITS file, or uses an unsupported format or compression mode.

  • Solution:

    • Verify the file opens correctly in other FITS viewers.

    • Ensure the file has a standard extension such as .fits or .fits.gz.

    • If it is a multi-extension FITS, ensure image data exists in at least one HDU.

A wrong image or header appears, or a previous file seems to persist

  • Problem: The preview shows a header or file that is not the one you just uploaded.

  • Solution:

    • Click Reset once. The uploader is re-created on every reset, so the previous file is dropped immediately; a second press is no longer needed.

    • Each browser session now works in its own work_<id> folder, so files of other users or tabs cannot leak into your analysis. If the problem persists, reload the page and report the file name and time.

    • Leftover temporary files from closed browsers or abandoned analyses are removed automatically after 24 hours; archived ZIP results are never deleted by this cleanup.

The FITS file uploads but nothing starts immediately

  • Problem: This is expected behavior in the current interface.

  • Solution:

    • Uploading stages the file only.

    • Click Start Analysis to trigger FITS loading, WCS checks, astrometry, and photometry.

Error: Missing required WCS keywords / WCS creation error

  • Problem: The FITS header lacks the necessary keywords for astropy.wcs to build a coordinate system.

  • Solution:

    • Enable plate solving using Astrometry.net.

    • Alternatively, use external software to add WCS information to the FITS header before uploading.

Astrometry Check / WCS Refinement Fails

  • Problem: The SCAMP refinement or blind-solving process could not find enough matches, or the initial WCS was too inaccurate.

  • Solution:

    • Ensure the initial WCS is roughly correct.

    • Ensure the scamp binary is installed and on PATH, or point RPP_SCAMP_EXECUTABLE at it. The refinement runs SCAMP directly.

    • Check internet connectivity when catalog access is needed.

    • Try adjusting the seeing parameter, as it affects detection.

    • The solver already lowers its detection threshold (3, 2, then 1 sigma) to reach about 20 stars (it also tries 2 sigma when 3 sigma gives fewer than 100 sources); fewer than 20 stars (or fewer than 5, which is fatal) means the field is too sparse, too short an exposure, or the image is saturated or out of focus.

    • If the field is very sparse or very crowded, refinement may struggle.

    • If Astrometry Check was enabled on an image that already had valid WCS, the app may fall back to the original WCS when the forced solve fails.

When the local Astrometry.net solve fails, RPP can optionally try the online Astrometry.net service using the detected source list (not the FITS image). Set ASTROMETRY_API_KEY in the environment of the Streamlit process, or configure api_key under [astrometry_net] in Astroquery’s ~/.astropy/config/astroquery.cfg. Online solving is skipped when no key is available; the original local-solve failure and WCS fallback behavior remain unchanged. Submitted source lists are marked private where supported by the service.

No Sources Found / Few Sources Found

  • Problem: Detection parameters may be unsuitable for the image.

  • Solution:

    • Lower the detection threshold to detect fainter sources.

    • Ensure the seeing estimate is reasonable.

    • Check if the border mask is too large.

    • Verify the image is not blank or excessively noisy.

Zero Point Calculation Fails / No Gaia Matches

  • Problem: The app could not match detected sources to the GAIA catalog or calculate a reliable zero point.

  • Solution:

    • Verify WCS accuracy.

    • Check internet connectivity for GAIA queries.

    • Adjust the filter magnitude limit.

    • Ensure the selected filter band is appropriate for the image filter.

    • The field may genuinely lack suitable GAIA stars in the specified magnitude range.

Unrealistic S/N or Magnitude Errors / Gain Reported as Ignored

  • Problem: The warning “… is outside the plausible effective-gain range” appears, or bright-source magnitude errors look far too small (and the cosmic-ray mask covers a large part of the frame). On several CMOS cameras the FITS GAIN keyword stores an abstract driver setting rather than an e-/ADU conversion factor: QHY uses a 0-100 scale (a QHY268M at GAIN=56 is ≈0.77 e-/ADU) and ZWO ASI uses a 0.1 dB value.

  • Solution:

    • RPP already recognises QHY/ZWO/ASI cameras (see DRIVER_GAIN_INSTRUMENT_PATTERNS) and ignores their bare GAIN, falling back to EGAIN/CVF, the frame’s photon-transfer estimate, or effective_gain = 1.

    • For the most accurate errors, set Detector Gain in the sidebar (or RPP_EFFECTIVE_GAIN for headless runs) to the true e-/ADU conversion factor for the gain setting in use, read from the manufacturer’s gain-vs-e-/ADU chart.

    • If the header carries a genuine conversion factor, provide it as EGAIN/CCDGAIN (e-/ADU) or CVF (RPP uses gain = 1/CVF).

Catalog Query Issues (SIMBAD, SkyBoT, etc.)

Warning: “Query failed: Network error / Timeout”

  • Problem: A temporary network issue occurred or the external catalog service is down or slow.

  • Solution:

    • Wait and try processing the image again later.

    • Check your internet connection.

    • Review the generated log file to see which catalog step timed out or was skipped.

    • Note that the pipeline may continue with partial results rather than failing completely.

Warning: “No sources found…” for a specific catalog

  • Problem: The catalog genuinely contains no known objects matching the criteria within your image field.

  • Solution: This is expected for many fields. The message is informational.

SkyBoT parse error: “not well-formed (invalid token)”

  • Problem: SkyBoT returned a malformed or non-XML payload for the query, so parsing failed.

  • Solution:

    • The pipeline now treats this as a warning and continues without SkyBoT matches.

    • Re-run later to retry the external service response.

    • If the preview starts with # Flag: -1, SkyBoT reports a service-side error. Keep the accompanying ticket number and report it to IMCCE if the error persists.

    • The pipeline requests VOTable output for Astroquery’s parser. A No sources found from 10 Parsec catalog message is a separate VizieR query result and is not caused by the SkyBoT response.

Astro-Colibri: No matches or Error

  • Problem: Invalid or missing API key, network issue, or no recent events in the field.

  • Solution:

    • Ensure you have entered the correct Astro-Colibri UID key in the sidebar.

    • Check internet connectivity.

    • Check the Astro-Colibri service status.

    • HTTP 429 means the daily quota (100 requests/day) is exhausted; the log message states the reason returned by the API.

    • A warning about the 15 or 20 arcsec tier means the association is loose: check it visually in Aladin.

Database and Migration Issues

Need to add 1.6.0 tracking tables to an existing database

  • Problem: Older databases may not contain the WCS FITS and ZIP archive tracking tables.

  • Solution:

    • Run python scripts/migrate_add_wcs_zip_tables.py.

    • Keep the generated backup before applying changes to production data.

Need to convert a legacy Streamlit SQLite database to the API schema

  • Problem: A legacy database layout may not match the SQLAlchemy-backed FastAPI schema.

  • Solution:

    • Run python scripts/migrate_legacy_db.py with the appropriate arguments.

    • Prefer a dry run and backup before migrating live data.

Pixel scale could not be determined

  • Problem: The run stops with “Pixel scale could not be determined from the FITS header”.

  • Solution: The header has no usable PIXSCALE/SECPIX, CD matrix, or pixel size + focal length, and the WCS could not provide a scale. Enter the value in the sidebar (Parameters > Pixel scale override, arcsec/pixel) and start the analysis again.

Login password not taken into account in Firefox

  • Problem: After typing the password, the value is not taken into account.

  • Solution: Press Enter in the password field before clicking Login.
